cards.statement: We are pleased to inform you that Meridian Industrials Fund IV has completed the sale of NorTech Industries to Brookfield Asset Management.

claims.claim: Meridian Industrials Fund IV has completed the sale of NorTech Industries to Brookfield Asset Management.
claims.comment: The source states that Fund IV completed the sale of NorTech Industries AB to Brookfield Asset Management; dropping 'AB' is acceptable paraphrase.

cards.statement: The transaction closed on 19 January 2026 at an enterprise value of SEK 18.4 billion, approximately EUR 1.62 billion.

claims.claim: The transaction closed on 19 January 2026 at an enterprise value of SEK 18.4 billion, approximately EUR 1.62 billion.
claims.comment: The source gives the same closing date, enterprise value, and euro equivalent.

cards.statement: The realisation generates gross proceeds to Fund IV of SEK 12.8 billion on invested capital of SEK 3.6 billion — a gross MOIC of 3.56x and a gross IRR of 31.4 percent over a 4.7-year hold.

claims.claim: The realisation generates gross proceeds to Fund IV of SEK 12.8 billion on invested capital of SEK 3.6 billion — a gross MOIC of 3.56x and a gross IRR of 31.4 percent over a 4.7-year hold.
claims.comment: All figures for gross proceeds, invested capital, MOIC, IRR, and hold period match the source.

cards.statement: Net to LPs after carry and expenses, the realisation delivers 2.74x net MOIC and 24.2 percent net IRR.

claims.claim: Net to LPs after carry and expenses, the realisation delivers 2.74x net MOIC and 24.2 percent net IRR.
claims.comment: The net MOIC and net IRR figures match the source; reference to carry and expenses is consistent with 'after Meridian carry and fund expenses'.

cards.statement: NorTech is the largest single realisation in Fund IV's history and moves the Fund's overall net IRR from 16.8 percent to 19.7 percent.

claims.claim: NorTech is the largest single realisation in Fund IV's history and moves the Fund's overall net IRR from 16.8 percent to 19.7 percent.
claims.comment: The source explicitly calls NorTech the largest single realisation and shows the net IRR moving from 16.8% to 19.7%.

cards.statement: International expansion took revenue contribution from outside the Nordic region from 19 percent at entry to 42 percent at exit.

claims.claim: International expansion took revenue contribution from outside the Nordic region from 19 percent at entry to 42 percent at exit.
claims.comment: At entry, 81% of revenue was from the Nordic region, implying 19% outside; at exit, international revenue is 42% of total. The statement correctly restates this as contribution from outside the Nordic region.

cards.statement: A modular product redesign drove gross margin from 28.4 percent to 34.1 percent.

claims.claim: A modular product redesign drove gross margin from 28.4 percent to 34.1 percent.
claims.comment: The source links the modularity programme to gross margin improvement from 28.4% to 34.1%; describing it as having 'drove' the change is acceptable paraphrase.

cards.statement: Four bolt-on acquisitions, anchored by HeatTech GmbH for SEK 1.1 billion, added meaningful scale.

claims.claim: Four bolt-on acquisitions, anchored by HeatTech GmbH for SEK 1.1 billion, added meaningful scale.
claims.comment: The source confirms four bolt-on acquisitions and that HeatTech GmbH was acquired for SEK 1.1 billion and added German presence and a complementary product line. However, the specific characterisation 'added meaningful scale' is not stated in the source and goes beyond the provided detail.

cards.statement: Manufacturing footprint optimisation and the new Polish facility completed the operational picture.

claims.claim: Manufacturing footprint optimisation and the new Polish facility completed the operational picture.
claims.comment: The source confirms manufacturing footprint optimisation and opening a new Polish facility, and that these drove margin and EBITDA improvements. The phrase 'completed the operational picture' is interpretive and not directly supported.

cards.statement: Total Company revenue grew from SEK 4.2 billion at entry to SEK 11.4 billion at exit, with EBITDA expanding from SEK 480 million to SEK 2.08 billion and margins from 11.4 percent to 18.2 percent.

claims.claim: Total Company revenue grew from SEK 4.2 billion at entry to SEK 11.4 billion at exit, with EBITDA expanding from SEK 480 million to SEK 2.08 billion and margins from 11.4 percent to 18.2 percent.
claims.comment: The revenue, EBITDA, and margin figures at entry and exit all match the source.

cards.statement: The exit process attracted seven preliminary offers, with Brookfield's SEK 18.4 billion bid meaningfully ahead of the next bid at SEK 16.9 billion.

claims.claim: The exit process attracted seven preliminary offers, with Brookfield's SEK 18.4 billion bid meaningfully ahead of the next bid at SEK 16.9 billion.
claims.comment: The source states there were seven preliminary offers and that Brookfield's SEK 18.4 billion offer was meaningfully ahead of the next bid at SEK 16.9 billion.

cards.statement: CEO Magnus Karlsson and the management team supported the Brookfield offer at the indicative stage; Brookfield's commitment to retain the Stockholm headquarters was an additional factor in the Company's preference.

claims.claim: CEO Magnus Karlsson and the management team supported the Brookfield offer at the indicative stage; Brookfield's commitment to retain the Stockholm headquarters was an additional factor in the Company's preference.
claims.comment: The source confirms both the management support at the indicative stage and Brookfield's commitment to retain the Stockholm headquarters as a factor in the company's preference.

cards.statement: With this realisation Fund IV becomes one of our strongest vintages.

claims.claim: With this realisation Fund IV becomes one of our strongest vintages.
claims.comment: The source states that with this realisation, Fund IV becomes one of the strongest vintages on a returns basis; the draft paraphrases this accurately.

cards.statement: Our focus turns to the three remaining portfolio companies and to deployment of Fund V, which closed in August 2025 at hard cap.

claims.claim: Our focus turns to the three remaining portfolio companies and to deployment of Fund V, which closed in August 2025 at hard cap.
claims.comment: The source notes three remaining portfolio companies and that Fund V closed in August 2025 at hard cap; the shift of focus is directly stated as well.

cards.statement: After more than four years of partnership, Meridian Capital has completed the sale of NorTech Industries to Brookfield this week.

claims.claim: After more than four years of partnership, Meridian Capital has completed the sale of NorTech Industries to Brookfield this week.
claims.comment: The completion of the sale of NorTech Industries to Brookfield this week is supported. The source does not mention 'more than four years of partnership' or specify the duration of ownership, so that part is not supported.

cards.statement: NorTech is a Stockholm-headquartered manufacturer of industrial heating and cooling systems, and when we invested in 2021 it was a strong but underexposed business — dominant in the Nordics and barely visible elsewhere.

claims.claim: NorTech is a Stockholm-headquartered manufacturer of industrial heating and cooling systems.
claims.comment: The source explicitly describes NorTech as Stockholm-headquartered and a manufacturer of industrial heating and cooling systems.

claims.claim: When we invested in 2021 it was a strong but underexposed business — dominant in the Nordics and barely visible elsewhere.
claims.comment: The source confirms acquisition in 2021 and that the company was strong but under-exposed outside Sweden, and constrained by a fragmented shareholder structure. However, it characterises NorTech as 'strong in Sweden, under-exposed everywhere else', not 'dominant in the Nordics and barely visible elsewhere'. The extension from Sweden to the broader Nordics is not supported.

cards.statement: The transformation since has been substantial.

claims.claim: The transformation since has been substantial.
claims.comment: The source describes NorTech evolving from a Sweden-focused company with constraints to a genuinely international business with a broad geographic footprint, which supports the characterisation of the transformation as substantial.

cards.statement: NorTech today operates across the Nordic region, Germany, France, the UK, and Poland, with international revenue having grown from a fifth of total revenue at entry to more than 40 percent at exit.

claims.claim: NorTech today operates across the Nordic region, Germany, France, the UK, and Poland.
claims.comment: The source states that four and a half years later NorTech is a genuinely international business with operations across the Nordic region, Germany, France, the UK, and Poland.

claims.claim: International revenue has grown from a fifth of total revenue at entry to more than 40 percent at exit.
claims.comment: The source discusses geographic expansion but provides no quantitative information on revenue mix or its change over time.

cards.statement: Total revenue grew nearly threefold over the hold period and EBITDA margins moved from 11 to 18 percent.

claims.claim: Total revenue grew nearly threefold over the hold period.
claims.comment: The source does not provide any figures or commentary on total revenue growth or multiples over the hold period.

claims.claim: EBITDA margins moved from 11 to 18 percent.
claims.comment: The source does not mention EBITDA margins or any margin figures.

cards.statement: The numbers tell one story; the team's transformation tells the bigger one.

claims.claim: The numbers tell one story; the team's transformation tells the bigger one.
claims.comment: While phrased rhetorically, this is consistent with the source’s emphasis on both the company’s internationalisation and the exceptional work of the team; it is a qualitative summary rather than a new factual claim.

cards.statement: Magnus Karlsson, who took on the international expansion challenge with grace and decisiveness.

claims.claim: Magnus Karlsson took on the international expansion challenge with grace and decisiveness.
claims.comment: The source explicitly credits Magnus Karlsson for taking on the international expansion challenge with grace and decisiveness.

cards.statement: Mikael Bergström, who navigated three generations of founding-family shareholder dynamics with patience and integrity.

claims.claim: Mikael Bergström navigated three generations of founding-family shareholder dynamics with patience and integrity.
claims.comment: The source states that Mikael Bergström, as chairman and bridge to the founding families, navigated three generations of shareholder dynamics with patience and integrity.

cards.statement: And the wider NorTech team across Stockholm and the new international footprint, who built something genuinely exceptional.

claims.claim: The wider NorTech team across Stockholm and the new international footprint built something genuinely exceptional.
claims.comment: The source credits the wider NorTech team in Stockholm and across the new international footprint with having built something exceptional; the addition of 'genuinely' is stylistic.

cards.statement: Excited to see what NorTech does next under Brookfield's ownership.

claims.claim: The author is excited to see what NorTech does next under Brookfield's ownership.
claims.comment: The source uses almost identical language expressing excitement about what NorTech will do next under Brookfield's ownership.

cards.statement: CloudPivot Systems (the "Company") is a London-headquartered vertical SaaS platform for the European freight forwarding industry.

claims.claim: CloudPivot Systems (the "Company") is a London-headquartered vertical SaaS platform for the European freight forwarding industry.
claims.comment: The source describes CloudPivot as London-headquartered and as a vertical SaaS platform serving the European logistics and freight forwarding industry, which supports this claim.

cards.statement: The transaction values the Company at an enterprise value of EUR 445 million.

claims.claim: The transaction values the Company at an enterprise value of EUR 445 million.
claims.comment: The memorandum states that the transaction values CloudPivot at an enterprise value of EUR 445 million.

cards.statement: The Company has built strong fundamentals.

claims.claim: The Company has built strong fundamentals.
claims.comment: The source provides financial and operating metrics but does not characterise them with the phrase "strong fundamentals" or an equivalent evaluative statement; this is an interpretive judgement not explicitly backed by the document.

cards.statement: It serves over 1'200 freight forwarder and customs broker customers across 28 European countries and generates annual recurring revenue (ARR) of EUR 84 million as of October 2025, up from EUR 52 million two years prior.

claims.claim: It serves over 1'200 freight forwarder and customs broker customers across 28 European countries and generates annual recurring revenue (ARR) of EUR 84 million as of October 2025, up from EUR 52 million two years prior.
claims.comment: The source confirms that CloudPivot serves over 1,200 freight forwarder and customs broker customers across 28 European countries and that ARR is EUR 84m as of October 2025, up from EUR 52m two years earlier.

cards.statement: EBITDA margin is 11.1% on trailing twelve months revenue of EUR 76 million.

claims.claim: EBITDA margin is 11.1% on trailing twelve months revenue of EUR 76 million.
claims.comment: The memorandum states trailing twelve months revenue of EUR 76m and EBITDA of EUR 8.4m, representing an EBITDA margin of 11.1%, matching this claim.

cards.statement: Net revenue retention has averaged 113% over the past 24 months.

claims.claim: Net revenue retention has averaged 113% over the past 24 months.
claims.comment: The source explicitly states that net revenue retention has averaged 113% over the past 24 months.

cards.statement: The team is led by founder-CEO Mr. Tom Fairfield and CTO Mr. James O'Brien.

claims.claim: The team is led by founder-CEO Mr. Tom Fairfield and CTO Mr. James O'Brien.
claims.comment: The document identifies Tom Fairfield as CEO and co-founder and James O'Brien as CTO and co-founder, supporting that they lead the team.

cards.statement: The Company employs 320 people across offices in London, Hamburg, Lisbon, and Bangalore.

claims.claim: The Company employs 320 people across offices in London, Hamburg, Lisbon, and Bangalore.
claims.comment: The source confirms the locations (London, Hamburg, Lisbon, Bangalore) but states that CloudPivot employs 320 people there, while a later section says the total team is 285. The employee count is internally inconsistent in the source; the claim matches one part but not the other.

cards.statement: It has built a clear competitive lead in the European mid-market against entrenched legacy software competitors.

claims.claim: It has built a clear competitive lead in the European mid-market against entrenched legacy software competitors.
claims.comment: The source discusses differentiation, competition from legacy software, and limited penetration of large global forwarders, but does not state that CloudPivot has a "clear competitive lead in the European mid-market"; this is an extrapolation beyond the text.

cards.statement: First, the European freight forwarding software market remains structurally underpenetrated, with approximately 40% of forwarders still on legacy systems or spreadsheets.

claims.claim: First, the European freight forwarding software market remains structurally underpenetrated, with approximately 40% of forwarders still on legacy systems or spreadsheets.
claims.comment: The memorandum notes that competition is mainly fragmented legacy software and that many products are aged with low satisfaction, but it does not quantify underpenetration or state that ~40% of forwarders are on legacy systems or spreadsheets.

cards.statement: Second, the Company's vertical product depth creates very high switching costs.

claims.claim: Second, the Company's vertical product depth creates very high switching costs.
claims.comment: The source emphasises ten years of domain investment and describes mission-critical software with very high switching costs due to integrations, supporting this claim about vertical product depth driving switching costs.

cards.statement: Third, the addressable European market of 14'000 forwarders gives meaningful headroom from the Company's current 8.6% penetration.

claims.claim: Third, the addressable European market of 14'000 forwarders gives meaningful headroom from the Company's current 8.6% penetration.
claims.comment: The memorandum states there are approximately 14,000 freight forwarders and customs brokers in Europe and that CloudPivot serves 1,200 (8.6% penetration), which implies significant remaining headroom; the term "meaningful" is a reasonable characterisation.

cards.statement: We project ARR growth from EUR 81 million today to approximately EUR 195 million over a five-year hold, representing 19% CAGR.

claims.claim: We project ARR growth from EUR 81 million today to approximately EUR 195 million over a five-year hold, representing 19% CAGR.
claims.comment: The source underwrites ARR growth from EUR 81m today to approximately EUR 195m over a five-year hold, representing 19% CAGR, matching this statement.

cards.statement: Our base case generates 2.6x MOIC and 21% gross IRR.

claims.claim: Our base case generates 2.6x MOIC and 21% gross IRR.
claims.comment: The memorandum states that the base case generates 2.6x MOIC and 21% IRR, but does not qualify it as "gross" IRR; the MOIC and IRR figures are supported, while the "gross" descriptor is not mentioned.

cards.statement: In summary, the Company is a high-quality vertical SaaS asset with a defensible competitive position.

claims.claim: In summary, the Company is a high-quality vertical SaaS asset with a defensible competitive position.
claims.comment: The conclusion describes CloudPivot as a high-quality vertical SaaS asset with a defensible competitive position, closely matching this summary.

cards.statement: The investment fits well with the broader portfolio strategy.

claims.claim: The investment fits well with the broader portfolio strategy.
claims.comment: The document does not discuss the broader portfolio strategy or how this investment fits within it; this linkage is not addressed in the source.

cards.statement: We are seeing increasing opportunity in European clinical decision support (CDS) software.

claims.claim: We are seeing increasing opportunity in European clinical decision support (CDS) software.
claims.comment: The memo sets out an investment thesis on European CDS software and describes it as a structurally attractive category at an inflection point, implying increasing opportunity.

cards.statement: The category — software that helps clinicians make better, faster, more consistent treatment decisions at the point of care — is at a structural inflection point driven by three forces.

claims.claim: The category — software that helps clinicians make better, faster, more consistent treatment decisions at the point of care — is at a structural inflection point driven by three forces.
claims.comment: The memo defines CDS similarly and explicitly states that the European market is at an inflection point due to three aligning forces; describing this as a structural inflection point is a reasonable paraphrase.

cards.statement: First, the regulatory pathway under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR) has matured.

claims.claim: First, the regulatory pathway under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR) has matured.
claims.comment: The source states that the regulatory pathway under EU MDR is now well‑understood, which supports describing it as having matured.

cards.statement: Incumbents with serious clinical software have built up meaningful regulatory clearances, creating real barriers to entry.

claims.claim: Incumbents with serious clinical software have built up meaningful regulatory clearances, creating real barriers to entry.
claims.comment: The memo notes that MDR has created higher barriers to entry for serious clinical software and that incumbents have built up significant clearances; this supports the claim that incumbents have meaningful clearances that create barriers to entry.

cards.statement: Second, payer willingness to reimburse digital health products has improved markedly across the major European markets.

claims.claim: Second, payer willingness to reimburse digital health products has improved markedly across the major European markets.
claims.comment: The source states that reimbursement codes for digital health products have improved meaningfully across major European markets and that payer willingness to reimburse CDS software has improved markedly; this directly supports the claim.

cards.statement: Third, generative AI is creating both opportunity and competitive pressure.

claims.claim: Third, generative AI is creating both opportunity and competitive pressure.
claims.comment: The memo says generative AI is creating both opportunity and pressure, which matches this statement.

cards.statement: The opportunity is for products that genuinely improve clinical workflows.

claims.claim: The opportunity is for products that genuinely improve clinical workflows.
claims.comment: The source specifies that generative AI offers opportunity to genuinely improve clinical workflows, which this sentence restates.

cards.statement: At the same time, generative AI is exposing incumbents that lack credible AI strategies to renewed competitive risk from challengers — and from each other.

claims.claim: At the same time, generative AI is exposing incumbents that lack credible AI strategies to renewed competitive risk from challengers — and from each other.
claims.comment: The memo notes that generative AI creates pressure on incumbents who lack credible AI strategies; describing this as exposing them to renewed competitive risk from challengers and peers is a reasonable elaboration of that pressure.

cards.statement: The European market is structurally distinct from the US in ways that favour a thoughtful financial sponsor.

claims.claim: The European market is structurally distinct from the US in ways that favour a thoughtful financial sponsor.
claims.comment: The memo explains structural distinctions between European and US markets and highlights features such as national payers, improved reimbursement, high regulatory barriers, fragmentation, and under‑serving by private equity, all of which favour a financial sponsor; this supports the claim.

cards.statement: National payers create clearer routes to scale once adopted by a national authority.

claims.claim: National payers create clearer routes to scale once adopted by a national authority.
claims.comment: The source states that European healthcare is dominated by national payers, which gives CDS products a clearer route to scale once adopted by a national authority; this is essentially verbatim.

cards.statement: The competitive landscape is fragmented across national markets, with leaders in the UK, Germany, France, and the Nordics but few players with meaningful pan-European presence — creating conditions for a buy-and-build strategy that pairs well with our M&A capabilities.

claims.claim: The competitive landscape is fragmented across national markets, with leaders in the UK, Germany, France, and the Nordics but few players with meaningful pan-European presence — creating conditions for a buy-and-build strategy that pairs well with our M&A capabilities.
claims.comment: The memo states that the European competitive landscape is fragmented across national markets, with national scale leaders in the UK, Germany, France, and the Nordics and few players with meaningful pan‑European presence, and that this creates conditions for a buy‑and‑build strategy that pairs well with the firm's M&A capabilities; the draft sentence closely follows this.

cards.statement: We expect to bring a specific potential investment to consider over the coming months.

claims.claim: We expect to bring a specific potential investment to consider over the coming months.
claims.comment: The memo says they plan to return within six months with either a specific transaction memo or a refreshed thesis and explicitly state they are not recommending any specific investment at this time. Expecting to bring a specific potential investment is more definitive than the source, which allows for the possibility that no specific investment will be ready and only a refreshed thesis will be provided.

cards.statement: We will provide further detail when the work is sufficiently advanced.

claims.claim: We will provide further detail when the work is sufficiently advanced.
claims.comment: The memo outlines a programme of work and states they plan to return to the Committee within six months with either a specific transaction memo or a refreshed thesis based on what they have learned, which supports the idea that further detail will be provided once the work has progressed.

claims.claim: We are writing to inform you of a new investment in Casa Verde Group (the "Company"), a Milan-headquartered premium European homeware and kitchenware specialist.
claims.comment: The source describes Casa Verde as Milan‑headquartered and as a premium European homeware and kitchenware retailer/brand owner, which supports this description and the fact it is an investment opportunity.

claims.claim: The transaction values the Company at an enterprise value of EUR 1.85 billion, representing 12.4x trailing twelve months EBITDA.
claims.comment: The memo states an enterprise value of EUR 1.85bn and that this represents 12.4x trailing twelve months EBITDA of EUR 149m.

cards.statement: We have invested EUR 720 million of equity for an 84% stake.

claims.claim: We have invested EUR 720 million of equity for an 84% stake.
claims.comment: The memo supports the EUR 720m equity amount and that Halden plus co‑investors together hold 84%. It does not support that EUR 720m alone buys an 84% stake; 84% is held by Halden and co‑investors combined.

cards.statement: The Company was founded in 1973 as a single shop in Milan.

claims.claim: The Company was founded in 1973 as a single shop in Milan.
claims.comment: The source states Casa Verde was founded in 1973 by Giovanni Esposito as a single homewares shop in Milan.

cards.statement: It today operates 184 retail stores across Italy, France, Spain, and Germany, alongside an e-commerce platform that contributes 31% of group revenue and a wholesale business serving design-led independent retailers across Europe.

claims.claim: It today operates 184 retail stores across Italy, France, Spain, and Germany, alongside an e-commerce platform that contributes 31% of group revenue and a wholesale business serving design-led independent retailers across Europe.
claims.comment: The memo confirms 184 stores in those four countries, e‑commerce at 31% of group revenue, and a wholesale business supplying independent design‑led homeware retailers across Europe.

cards.statement: Revenue in 2025 was EUR 612 million with EBITDA margins of 24.3%.

claims.claim: Revenue in 2025 was EUR 612 million with EBITDA margins of 24.3%.
claims.comment: The memo states 2025 revenue of EUR 612m and EBITDA of EUR 149m, a margin of 24.3%.

cards.statement: Category leadership in the EUR 38 billion European premium homeware market — a structurally attractive category growing at 4-5% annually.

claims.claim: Category leadership in the EUR 38 billion European premium homeware market — a structurally attractive category growing at 4-5% annually.
claims.comment: The memo describes premium homeware in Europe as a EUR 38bn market growing at 4–5% annually and notes Casa Verde’s category‑leading market share, supporting the idea of category leadership in that market.

cards.statement: Exceptional store unit economics — average four-wall EBITDA margins of 22% (meaning the EBITDA generated by each individual store before head-office costs) and 2.4-year payback on new store openings.

claims.claim: Exceptional store unit economics — average four-wall EBITDA margins of 22% (meaning the EBITDA generated by each individual store before head-office costs) and 2.4-year payback on new store openings.
claims.comment: The memo states average four‑wall store EBITDA margin of 22% and payback on new store openings of 2.4 years. The parenthetical explanation is definitional and does not contradict the source.

cards.statement: A well-defined international expansion runway — the Company has executed successful launches in France, Spain, and Germany, and we plan to enter the UK, Netherlands, and Nordics.

claims.claim: A well-defined international expansion runway — the Company has executed successful launches in France, Spain, and Germany, and we plan to enter the UK, Netherlands, and Nordics.
claims.comment: The memo describes the playbook executed in France, Spain, and Germany and identifies the UK, Netherlands, and Nordics as the next logical markets with planned store openings there.

cards.statement: Continued own-brand penetration uplift — own-brand share has grown from 38% in 2020 to 54% in 2025, with continued runway to 70% contributing material gross margin expansion.

claims.claim: Continued own-brand penetration uplift — own-brand share has grown from 38% in 2020 to 54% in 2025, with continued runway to 70% contributing material gross margin expansion.
claims.comment: The memo gives own‑brand penetration rising from 38% to 54%, a path to 70%, and that this contributes about 250 bps of gross margin expansion, supporting the claim of material margin uplift.

cards.statement: The Atelier 73 growth concept — Atelier 73 is the Company's smaller, design-led store format positioned at a younger urban customer.

claims.claim: The Atelier 73 growth concept — Atelier 73 is the Company's smaller, design-led store format positioned at a younger urban customer.
claims.comment: The memo describes Atelier 73 as small‑format stores targeting younger urban customers with a curated, design‑led assortment, matching this characterisation.

claims.claim: The format currently operates 18 stores and represents a fifth value driver alongside the four pillars above.

cards.statement: Atelier 73 has potential to become a meaningful growth pillar.

claims.claim: Atelier 73 has potential to become a meaningful growth pillar.

cards.statement: Our value creation plan envisages revenue growth from EUR 612 million to approximately EUR 1.04 billion by 2031, a 9.2% CAGR.

claims.comment: The memo states revenue growth from EUR 612m in 2025 to about EUR 1.04bn in 2031, a 9.2% CAGR.

claims.comment: The memo gives EBITDA of EUR 149m in 2025, growing to about EUR 295m by 2031 with margins expanding from 24.3% to 28.4%.

cards.statement: The base case generates 2.7x MOIC and 22% gross IRR.

claims.claim: The base case generates 2.7x MOIC and 22% gross IRR.
claims.comment: The memo states that the base case generates a 2.7x MOIC and 22% gross IRR.

cards.statement: The principal risks are well understood and reflected in our planning.

claims.comment: The memo identifies principal risks, describes mitigations and stress‑testing, and notes that principal risks are well‑understood with specific mitigations built into the approach, supporting this summary statement.

cards.statement: The UK and Nordic launches are the largest single contributor to growth.

claims.claim: The UK and Nordic launches are the largest single contributor to growth.
claims.comment: The memo notes that international expansion, primarily from UK and Nordic launches, is a principal driver of growth and that international expansion contributes the largest single block of incremental EBITDA, supporting this characterisation.

cards.statement: We have direct experience of homeware concepts that have failed in the UK market and have mitigated through detailed commercial diligence, a phased rollout, and a recruited UK country manager subject to deal completion.

claims.claim: We have direct experience of homeware concepts that have failed in the UK market and have mitigated through detailed commercial diligence, a phased rollout, and a recruited UK country manager subject to deal completion.
claims.comment: The memo cites experience with failed UK homeware concepts, detailed commercial diligence, a phased rollout, and identification of an experienced UK retail country manager who has agreed to join subject to deal completion.

claims.claim: The Company's discretionary positioning means demand sensitivity to macroeconomic conditions.
claims.comment: The memo describes homeware as a discretionary purchase and discusses stress‑testing for consumer downturns, implying demand sensitivity to macro conditions.

claims.claim: Germany has been notably weak in 2025, while Italy and Spain remain strong.

cards.statement: We have stress-tested the model for sustained German weakness and the returns remain attractive.

claims.claim: We have stress-tested the model for sustained German weakness and the returns remain attractive.

claims.claim: Marco Esposito will step back from day-to-day responsibilities post-close, with Elena Conti (current COO and 17-year company veteran) becoming CEO.
claims.comment: The memo states Marco will step back from day‑to‑day responsibilities post‑close, remain Chairman, and that current COO Elena Conti, a 17‑year company veteran, will assume the CEO role.

cards.statement: Reference checks have been comprehensive and uniformly positive.

claims.claim: Reference checks have been comprehensive and uniformly positive.
claims.comment: The memo explicitly notes that reference checks on Elena have been comprehensive and uniformly positive.

cards.statement: 167 of 184 stores are leased with average remaining term of 7.2 years.

claims.claim: 167 of 184 stores are leased with average remaining term of 7.2 years.
claims.comment: The memo states that the company leases 167 of its 184 store locations with a weighted average remaining term of 7.2 years.

claims.claim: In light of the overall good performance of the portfolio, 3i declared a dividend of GBP 0.365 per share, which will be paid in January 2026.
claims.comment: The dividend amount (36.5p per share) and payment timing (January 2026) are confirmed. The source does not state that the dividend was declared “in light of the overall good performance of the portfolio”; that causal framing is not supported.

cards.statement: Looking ahead, management maintains its cautious stance on capital deployment into new investments, but remains open to selective allocations to lower-risk reinvestments in existing portfolio companies.

claims.claim: Looking ahead, management maintains its cautious stance on capital deployment into new investments, but remains open to selective allocations to lower-risk reinvestments in existing portfolio companies.
claims.comment: The source states that 3i remains cautious in deploying capital into new investment and will continue to allocate selectively, including to lower-risk reinvestments in businesses it knows and trusts. This matches the claim’s substance.

cards.statement: HICL Infrastructure’s performance for the five months to 28 February 2026 was positive and largely in line with expectations.

claims.claim: HICL Infrastructure’s performance for the five months to 28 February 2026 was positive and largely in line with expectations.
claims.comment: The period covered is 1 October 2025 to 28 February 2026 (five months), and the source repeatedly states that portfolio performance, NAV performance, cash generation, and EBITDA are in line with expectations, which reasonably supports describing performance as positive and largely in line with expectations.

cards.statement: Across the portfolio, operational performance was robust, with EBITDA growth driven by capital expenditure, and resilient cashflow generation supporting HCIL’s dividend program.

claims.claim: Across the portfolio, operational performance was robust, with EBITDA growth driven by capital expenditure, and resilient cashflow generation supporting HCIL’s dividend program.
claims.comment: The source supports that operational performance was robust/in line with expectations, that capex programmes are driving EBITDA growth, and that cash generation underpins dividend cover and the dividend outlook. However, the draft misspells the company as “HCIL” rather than HICL, which is not supported by the source and is an error, so the claim is only partially confirmed.

cards.statement: Across the portfolio, growth investments continue to perform well, with significant investment in expansion programs driving EBITDA growth that continues to perform in line with budgets.

claims.claim: Across the portfolio, growth investments continue to perform well, with significant investment in expansion programs driving EBITDA growth that continues to perform in line with budgets.
claims.comment: The source states that HICL’s growth investments continue to perform well, that they are progressing significant expansion capex programmes, and that EBITDA is in line with expectations. This supports the paraphrase about growth investments performing well and expansion programmes driving EBITDA growth in line with budgets.

cards.statement: Among the significant holdings, London St. Pancras High Speed performed well during the period, with international train path bookings slightly ahead of forecast.

claims.claim: Among the significant holdings, London St. Pancras High Speed performed well during the period, with international train path bookings slightly ahead of forecast.
claims.comment: The source explicitly notes that London St. Pancras High Speed performed well in the period and that international train path bookings were slightly ahead of forecast, matching the claim.

cards.statement: On the commercial front, progress has been made on adding a second international operator on the route, while Virgin Trains recently announced its intentions for cross-Channel operations from St. Pancras.

claims.claim: On the commercial front, progress has been made on adding a second international operator on the route, while Virgin Trains recently announced its intentions for cross-Channel operations from St. Pancras.
claims.comment: The source describes further progress toward a potential second international operator, including announcements by Virgin Trains regarding its intentions for cross-Channel operations from St. Pancras. This supports the claim, which is a faithful paraphrase.

cards.statement: Elsewhere, Fortysouth delivered 16 new towers during the period and is actively progressing additional co-location opportunities, both of which are expected to support continued growth in EBITDA and valuation gains.

claims.claim: Elsewhere, Fortysouth delivered 16 new towers during the period and is actively progressing additional co-location opportunities, both of which are expected to support continued growth in EBITDA and valuation gains.
claims.comment: The source confirms that Fortysouth delivered 16 new towers, is progressing incremental co-location opportunities, and that these are expected to support continued EBITDA growth in line with valuation assumptions. However, the draft adds “and valuation gains,” which is not stated in the source. The EBITDA aspect is supported; the explicit reference to valuation gains is not, so the claim is only partially confirmed.

cards.statement: The company also recently completed an oversubscribed refinancing, which will lead to a reduction in debt servicing costs.

claims.claim: The company also recently completed an oversubscribed refinancing, which will lead to a reduction in debt servicing costs.
claims.comment: The source confirms that Fortysouth completed an accretive refinancing that was about 30% oversubscribed and that this enabled a step-down in debt margins earlier than forecast. Oversubscription and a reduction in debt margins are supported. However, the statement that this “will lead to a reduction in debt servicing costs” is an inference not explicitly made in the source, so that part is not directly supported, making the claim partially confirmed.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, Affinity Water appointed a new CEO with significant sector experience and stands to benefit from the UK government’s recently published white paper on water sector reform.

claims.claim: Meanwhile, Affinity Water appointed a new CEO with significant sector experience and stands to benefit from the UK government’s recently published white paper on water sector reform.
claims.comment: The source confirms that Affinity Water appointed Mark Garth as CEO and that he has significant sector experience. It also notes that many aspects of the UK Government’s water sector reform white paper are expected to be beneficial for strong performers such as Affinity Water. However, the draft’s unqualified “stands to benefit” generalises this expectation; the source is more conditional and framed around strong performers. Thus, the CEO and experience elements are confirmed, while the simplified benefit claim is only partially supported.

cards.statement: In November 2025, GP Industries announced that it intends to shift production capacity to its manufacturing sites in Southeast Asia to serve the US market amid tariffs and rising geopolitical tensions.

claims.claim: In November 2025, GP Industries announced that it intends to shift production capacity to its manufacturing sites in Southeast Asia to serve the US market amid tariffs and rising geopolitical tensions.
claims.comment: The press release is dated 13 November 2025 and states that GP Industries, the world’s second-largest producer of consumer batteries, is shifting production capacity to its Southeast Asia facilities to serve the US market in response to US tariffs and rising geopolitical tensions. The wording "announced that it intends to" is a reasonable paraphrase of the press release itself.

cards.statement: The company currently operates three facilities in Malaysia, two in Vietnam, and one in Thailand, alongside two other plants in the UK and one plant in China, which will now focus primarily on the European and Asian markets.

claims.claim: The company currently operates three facilities in Malaysia, two in Vietnam, and one in Thailand, alongside two other plants in the UK and one plant in China, which will now focus primarily on the European and Asian markets.
claims.comment: The source confirms three facilities in Malaysia, two in Vietnam, one in Thailand, and two other plants in the UK, and that the China facility will now focus primarily on the European and Asian markets. However, the draft adds "one plant in China" as an operational detail, which is not stated in the source; the source only refers to "its China facility" without specifying the number of plants.

cards.statement: The capacity adjustments are intended to streamline supply chains to meet country-of-origin requirements while maintaining cost competitiveness.

claims.claim: The capacity adjustments are intended to streamline supply chains to meet country-of-origin requirements while maintaining cost competitiveness.
claims.comment: The source explains that production capacity in Southeast Asia will be ramped up to serve the US market while the China facility focuses on Europe and Asia, and explicitly states that this move will streamline supply chains to meet country-of-origin requirements and maintain cost competitiveness.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, Gold Peak Technology (parent of GP Industries) is planning an investment program in Johor, Malaysia, to produce next-generation batteries to support data centres.

claims.claim: Meanwhile, Gold Peak Technology (parent of GP Industries) is planning an investment program in Johor, Malaysia, to produce next-generation batteries to support data centres.
claims.comment: The source confirms that GP Industries is owned 86.18% by Hong Kong-listed Gold Peak Technology Group and that this parent is planning a multi-million-dollar investment in Johor to produce next-generation battery to support data centres. The draft’s description of Gold Peak Technology as the parent and its Johor investment is supported, but the term "investment program" and the explicit mention of "Malaysia" are not in the source; Johor is named without country, and the nature of the investment as a "program" is an extrapolation.

cards.statement: GP Industries is the second-largest producer of consumer batteries globally, producing over 6 billion batteries annually, which are sold through 1 million outlets worldwide.

claims.claim: GP Industries is the second-largest producer of consumer batteries globally, producing over 6 billion batteries annually, which are sold through 1 million outlets worldwide.
claims.comment: The source describes GP Industries as the world’s second-largest producer of consumer batteries and states that it produces over six billion batteries annually, sold through one million outlets worldwide. The draft’s wording is a faithful paraphrase.

cards.statement: In May 2026, ClearPoint Neuro reported its financial results for the first quarter of 2026.

claims.claim: In May 2026, ClearPoint Neuro reported its financial results for the first quarter of 2026.
claims.comment: The press release is dated May 13, 2026 and announces financial results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026.

cards.statement: The company delivered 43% year-on-year growth in revenue to USD 12.1 million, driven by an expansion of the activated installed base to more than 175 global centers and ongoing integration of the recently-acquired IRRAflow product portfolio.

claims.claim: The company delivered 43% year-on-year growth in revenue to USD 12.1 million.
claims.comment: The source reports Q1 2026 revenue of $12.1 million versus $8.5 million in Q1 2025, an increase of $3.6 million or 43%.

claims.claim: The 43% year-on-year growth in revenue was driven by an expansion of the activated installed base to more than 175 global centers and ongoing integration of the recently-acquired IRRAflow product portfolio.
claims.comment: The source confirms the activated installed base is over 175 centers and that integration of the IRRAflow portfolio is achieving synergies, but it does not state that these factors *drove* the 43% revenue growth. The causal framing is not supported.

cards.statement: Organic growth amounted to 16% year on year (25% for devices), while the gross margin expanded to 64% over the period on account of lower allowances for excess and obsolete inventory.

claims.claim: Organic growth amounted to 16% year on year.
claims.comment: The highlights state 16% year-over-year total organic growth compared with Q1 2025.

claims.claim: Organic growth amounted to 25% year on year for devices.
claims.comment: The release headline and CEO commentary reference 25% organic growth in devices; this supports 25% year-on-year organic growth for devices.

claims.claim: The gross margin expanded to 64% over the period on account of lower allowances for excess and obsolete inventory.
claims.comment: The source reports gross margin of 64% for Q1 2026 versus 60% in Q1 2025 and attributes the increase primarily to lower excess and obsolete inventory.

cards.statement: Topline growth was driven by the neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access division, which achieved an 80% increase in revenue to USD 5.9 million, benefitting from contributions from the IRRAflow product line and the 3.0 operating room navigation software.

claims.claim: Topline growth was driven by the neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access division, which achieved an 80% increase in revenue to USD 5.9 million.
claims.comment: The source confirms neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access revenue increased 80% to $5.9 million. However, it does not state that overall topline growth was *driven* by this division; that causal attribution is not explicitly supported.

claims.claim: The neurosurgery navigation, therapy and access division benefitted from contributions from the IRRAflow product line and the 3.0 operating room navigation software.
claims.comment: The source attributes the revenue increase in this category to additional revenues from IRRAflow product sales and the introduction of the 3.0 operating room navigation software.

cards.statement: Capital equipment and software revenue increased by 177% from a low base due to an increase in placements of ClearPoint navigation capital and software, IRRAflow control units, and Prism laser units.

claims.claim: Capital equipment and software revenue increased by 177% from a low base due to an increase in placements of ClearPoint navigation capital and software, IRRAflow control units, and Prism laser units.
claims.comment: The source confirms a 177% increase in capital equipment and software revenue and attributes it to increased placements of ClearPoint navigation capital and software, IRRAflow control units, and Prism laser units. The description of the prior period as a "low base" is not stated in the source and is interpretive.

cards.statement: Meanwhile, biologics and drug delivery revenue was broadly flat compared with the prior year.

claims.claim: Biologics and drug delivery revenue was broadly flat compared with the prior year.
claims.comment: The source shows biologics and drug delivery revenue increasing from $4.7 million to $4.8 million and describes the increase as slight, which supports the characterization as broadly flat.

claims.claim: The company continues to progress its clinical trial program, which now covers more than 60 active biopharma partners.
claims.comment: The highlights note continued clinical trial and regulatory progress across more than 60 active biopharma partners, and the CEO reiterates a portfolio of more than 60 partners and programs.

cards.statement: Notably, FDA clearance was received and first clinical procedures completed utilizing the company's Velocity Alpha MR High Speed Surgical Drill System.

claims.claim: FDA clearance was received and first clinical procedures completed utilizing the company's Velocity Alpha MR High Speed Surgical Drill System.
claims.comment: The source states FDA clearance and successful completion of the first clinical procedure using the Velocity Alpha MR High Speed Surgical Drill System, and the CEO notes the drill has now been used clinically for the first time.

cards.statement: Elsewhere, Health Canada issued a medical device license for the ClearPoint Neuro Navigation System, which covers both MRI-guidance and iCT guidance workflows, while the first commercial drug delivery case utilizing ClearPoint technology was completed in the Asia-Pacific region.

claims.claim: Health Canada issued a medical device license for the ClearPoint Neuro Navigation System, which covers both MRI-guidance and iCT guidance workflows, while the first commercial drug delivery case utilizing ClearPoint technology was completed in the Asia-Pacific region.
claims.comment: The source confirms receipt of a Medical Device License from Health Canada for the ClearPoint Neuro Navigation System covering MRI and iCT workflows, and completion of the first commercial drug delivery case in the Asia-Pacific region.

cards.statement: The company provided updated revenue guidance of USD 52-56 million for 2026.

claims.comment: The Business Outlook section states estimated 2026 revenue between $52.0 million and $56.0 million; the draft’s wording as guidance is consistent with this.
